prompt:
Does any thread of crunch stay runnable but get almost no CPU time for a long stretch (seconds)? If so, which thread, and what keeps it off the CPU?

Begin your answer with exactly one line: "Verdict: yes", "Verdict: no", or "Verdict: cannot tell from this trace". Then answer the question.
answer:
Verdict: no

Across the trace (0–30,613.940 ms), none of the measured crunch threads had a seconds-long runnable wait. For calc-1, runnable waiting totaled 39.797 ms over about 29.9 seconds; its longest wait after a wake-up was 0.737 ms, and its longest wait after preemption was 1.888 ms.

The per-round profile also shows only 0.004–0.122 ms waiting for CPU per round across calc-0 through calc-7. For calc-1, the CPU was idle or handling interrupts for most of its measured runnable-wait time; other threads held it for only small shares.
